items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: So finally, he would play with this Jameson guy, and I would too

ctx.x: as music but now if they're so much over me and you have to live like that, well I just couldn't see it and I didn't go.

Well anyway, I'm still not with any band and don't have anything else around there, so the next thing that came up, before it became any band time or anything, Jameson-- I don't remember Jameson's first name. They brought him into the theatre just to play for those silent pictures--a piano player. He would play and get little gigs on the side and that's how Butterbeans and Susie were going on when this Jameson came in. He would get some of the musicians--whenever he would get a little gig--to play with him, and…

can play a horn, and I said I can too. So he said we got to get together then and I said yeah. It was in the summertime then, and hot and the wiring, crawling up into the attic on the job and he said, man, I think I can get you something better than this. So I said what. He said I was playing with the Missourians, and they have told me that a guy has brought in (inaudible); an entertainer, a vocalist, that is a terrific showman and they have money behind them, and says they're going to call me. He said will you…
